summary: Specifies the Discard service, which throws away any data it receives. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

eli5.summary: A computer that listens to everything you send and then ignores it, like a bottomless bin.

subtitle: A tiny service that silently throws away whatever it receives, used as a debugging and measurement tool.

tldr.problem: Operators need a very simple data sink for debugging and measuring a network path.
tldr.mechanism: A discard service throws away any data it receives and sends no response, on port 9 over either TCP or UDP.
tldr.outcome: Hosts that choose to implement a Discard Protocol are expected to follow this standard.

today: RFC 863 is an Internet Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What a Discard Service Is
sections.content: The RFC calls a discard service a useful debugging and measurement tool. It simply throws away any data it receives. Hosts that choose to implement a Discard Protocol are expected to adopt this standard; implementing it is optional.
sections.eli5: You send it stuff and it never sends anything back.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Discard
sections.content:
The TCP-based service is connection based. A server listens for TCP connections on port 9. Once a connection is established, any data received is thrown away and no response is sent. This continues until the calling user terminates the connection.

The UDP-based service is datagram based. A server listens for UDP datagrams on port 9. When a datagram is received, it is thrown away and no response is sent.
sections.eli5: Over a phone call it listens until you hang up and says nothing. For postcards it reads each one and drops it in the bin.

sections.title: Standard Status
sections.content: RFC 863 is an Internet Standard from May 1983. The text defines only the two port 9 behaviors above.
sections.eli5: It is a listener that never answers: everything sent to it just disappears.
